findings.impact: The staleness contract measures producer liveness, not data freshness. If some or all fetchers fail, the UI shows a current-dated, fresh-looking chart whose tail is frozen carry-forward and the staleness banner never fires — the most likely mechanical cause of 'expected data missing' on any deployment where the shadowing of finding 008 does not apply. findings.recommendation: Extend staleness to max(raw_date) per panel: flag any indicator whose last real observation lags more than N days, flag the composite when more than k indicators lag, and color stale Last cells on the regime page.

runtime (observed 2026-07-31, stack rm_demo_stack_d2b89936a0): 140 regime_snapshots rows dated 2026-08-01..2026-12-18, growing +1 per demo session; GET /api/dashboards/regime-snapshots?range=30 returned a window entirely of future dates with latest 2026-12-19; GET /api/committee/open-session returned date 2026-12-20
findings.impact: Root cause of the reported missing data on stage: ~140 future-dated demo-cadence snapshots shadow all real current rows in every newest-N window (the genuine 2026-07-31 row sits ~141 rows deep), the regime badge shows a Dec-2026 synthetic neutral reading, and the staleness guard passes because future data is 'not stale'. Same mechanism dates committee sessions months ahead. This resolves the open-question in issue #345: it is the generator (candidate 2 — reproduces on every fresh demo), not clock skew, and the fast demo cadence (~1 session/76s) accumulated 5 months of virtual dates in 6 hours.
findings.recommendation: Bound fetchRegimeSnapshots (and staleness asof) to date <= server date; stop demo committee sessions writing future-asof classifications into the shared regime_snapshots table (isolate the virtual-date rail or clamp asof); add the no-future-rows guard test issue #345 specifies; clean the future-dated rows on the stage database.
